approvedConcept: User approved slim, fast swordsman concept on 2026-10-21.

assets.prompt: Use the attached ORIGINAL approved concept sheet as the character identity reference. Create a production-ready transparent-background cutout of ONLY the larger standing swordsman on the LEFT of this sheet. Preserve his exact slim athletic anatomy, face, loosely tied long black ponytail, light black kimono, gathered hakama, grey sash, wrapped ankles, sandals, restrained red sash tails, worn ink textures and low held curved katana. Keep his full body, sword, scabbard, hair and cloth in frame, with modest transparent padding. Face and sword extend LEFT: mirror the character as necessary so he looks toward the left of the final canvas. Pose calm, graceful and ready to move, not squatting. Refine his fingers and katana grip without redesigning his costume. Keep the katana attached to the correct hand, blade clear of his legs. Do not add armour, helmet, horns, bow, scenery, rocks, ink floor, separate small figure, paper texture, title or symbols. Remove ALL paper/background completely. Maintain truly transparent alpha between hair strands, around hems and between legs. No white halo, no dark rectangular panel, no checkerboard baked into the pixels, no watermark. This will be composited over a coloured sunset in the game's main menu. Full-body single-character artwork, high detail and hand-painted sumi-e wash, not a geometric approximation.

Use the attached ORIGINAL approved slim wandering swordsman concept as identity and costume reference. Transform it into a professional 2D skeletal-animation body-part atlas on a TRULY TRANSPARENT background. Square canvas; exactly 4 columns by 4 rows of equal invisible cells, evenly spaced with ample transparent padding in each cell. Sixteen isolated painted parts, no assembled figures, no paper, no grid lines, no captions or letters. All pieces share the same dark charcoal brush-painted kimono, natural grey wash folds, muted neutral skin and restrained red accents. Character faces RIGHT. Parts may overlap their intended joint slightly when assembled. Row 1 left-to-right: (1) ONLY head and short neck, right-facing profile, dark hair tied high, loose fringe, small subtle nose and jaw, NO helmet and NO long trailing ponytail; head upright with neck at bottom. (2) ONLY slim kimono torso from shoulder collar to waist sash, upright, narrow waist, deep V overlapping pale-grey lapels, absolutely NO head, arms or legs. (3) ONLY the waist/short parted robe skirt with grey sash knot and scabbard angled back left, upright, lower hem splits into a few trailing brush tips; NO torso, head, limbs, belt beyond this one cell or long sword. (4) ONLY detached long black ponytail flowing LEFT from its tied attachment point at the RIGHT, a thin sinuous graceful brush silhouette, no head. Row 2 left-to-right: (1) near upper arm sleeve, (2) near forearm including small hand, (3) near upper leg in slim gathered black hakama, (4) near lower leg with narrow ankle wraps, NO FOOT. All row 2 limb segments are HORIZONTAL, proximal joint at LEFT and distal joint at RIGHT, built to rotate in a 2D skeleton; upper arm has softly hanging black kimono sleeve cloth, forearm has wrist wraps with hand at extreme RIGHT, upper leg cloth wider at LEFT tapering toward knee at RIGHT. Row 3 left-to-right: (1) far upper arm sleeve, (2) far forearm including hand, (3) far upper leg, (4) far lower leg with wraps and NO FOOT; exactly like row 2 but slightly darker for depth, ALL HORIZONTAL with proximal joint LEFT and distal joint RIGHT. Row 4 left-to-right: (1) near sandal foot, flat sole at bottom, toes point RIGHT, ankle joins near the LEFT THIRD, (2) far sandal foot same orientation, (3) a thin dark red cloth tail trailing LEFT from an attachment at RIGHT, (4) a slender horizontal curved katana with the handle at LEFT and the blade tip pointing RIGHT, no hand. Each painted part fills roughly 70 to 80 percent of its cell's width or height; keep invisible cell boundaries absolutely empty so pieces can be extracted independently. Full real transparency and meaningful negative space; no drop shadows, ground lines, white halos, checkerboard pixels or rectangles. Prioritize lean connected clothing and natural anatomy, NOT samurai armour, big shoulder pads, disconnected robotic rectangles or extremely tiny sticks. These are game animation source assets: anatomically coherent, neatly separated, consistent painterly identity, no scenery or text.
